options.lead: You are now the size of a quarter.
lines: Six stations. Every exhibit is a live money model.
Click one, press Program, change a number.
options.footnote: Rates here are classroom examples, not predictions or financial advice

options.subtitle: What you earn is not what you get

options.title: The take-home model
options.caption: Click the coin stack, press Program, change the wage.

options.title: Your W-4 sets the withholding
options.body: FICA is 7.65%, set by law. Income tax depends on your W-4 and is settled when you file. Withhold too much and you get a refund, which is your own money coming back.

options.title: A new bracket will not cut your pay
options.body: Brackets are marginal: a higher rate applies only to the dollars above the line, not to all of your pay. Moving into a new bracket does not shrink what you already had.

options.subtitle: A budget is a plan you write before the month

options.footer: Nothing here is expensive. That is how it works.

options.title: What small charges add up to
options.caption: Click the receipt. Put in what you really pay for.

options.eyebrow: A STARTING POINT, NOT A RULE
options.title: 50 / 30 / 20 on $1,100 a month
options.note: Where rent takes more than half, the split has to bend. A budget that fits your life beats one that fits the rule.

options.title: Each plan looks small on its own
options.body: Five $100 purchases split into 4 payments is $125.00 due every two weeks: 25% of the paycheck at Station 1, before rent.

options.title: Build your budget as a bar
options.intro: Menu > Create Model. Make one bar for $1,100 a month, 1ft for every $100. The ruler's numbers are 5ft apart.

steps.text: A second Cube, 3.3ft. Lift it onto the first with the green ball.
A third, 2.2ft, on top. Then Connect and Render Model.

options.tip: Now rent goes up $100. Which block shrinks? That choice IS your budget.

options.subtitle: Time does more of the work than you do

options.title: Invested at 18
options.body: Every $1 becomes $24.05 by 65. Read its height on the ruler, not its bulk: it grows in every direction, so it looks bigger than it is.

options.title: Invested at 28
options.body: Every $1 becomes $12.22 by 65. Ten years later, about half as much.

options.title: Compounding is one line
options.caption: Click a sprout. Change startAge or rate. Press Save.

options.eyebrow: $100 A MONTH AT 7% (AN EXAMPLE, NOT A PROMISE)
options.title: Starting ten years sooner
options.note: Money doubles about every 10 years at 7%: the rule of 72, 72 / 7. Check it against the sprouts.

options.title: Cash in a drawer melts
options.body: At 3% a year, $100 buys only $49 worth of today's stuff after 24 years. Saving keeps your money. Beating inflation is what keeps its value.

options.title: Grow $1 for ten years
options.target: Click the third sprout (no green arrow), press Program, stay in Block Code:
options.tip: change size by 7 multiplies by 1.07, which IS 7% interest. After ten rounds it has about doubled. Press the green arrow, then try 1%.

options.subtitle: Compounding works against you just as hard

options.title: The debt model
options.caption: Click the balloon, change the payment, press Save.

options.eyebrow: $500 ON A CARD AT 24% APR (AN EXAMPLE)
options.title: The payment decides everything
options.note: A minimum payment is what the lender needs from you, not what you need to pay.

options.title: What goes into a credit score
options.note: Landlords and insurers may check your credit too. You can get your reports free at annualcreditreport.com.

options.eyebrow: THE SAME $20,000 CAR, TWO EXAMPLE LOANS
options.title: The lower payment costs more
options.note: A dealer who asks "what payment can you afford?" is not asking about the total.

options.subtitle: Plan for the thing you cannot predict

options.title: The emergency model
options.caption: Click the coins in the jar. Change insured. Press Save.

options.title: Why people pay for insurance
options.note: Insure what you could not afford to replace. A lost $20 charger is not worth a policy; a car crash is.

options.title: Count the red flags
options.body: Urgency. A threat. A prize you never entered for. A request for a password or Social Security number. No real bank asks for those by text. Go to the real site yourself.

options.title: Freezing your credit is free
options.body: A credit freeze stops new accounts being opened in your name, and federal law makes it free at all three bureaus. Deposits at an FDIC-insured bank are covered up to $250,000 per depositor.

options.title: Make savings react to an accident
options.target: Click the coins in the YOUR TURN jar, press Program, stay in Block Code:

steps.text: say Half my savings are gone

options.tip: The mug says "accident" every 12 seconds. Any object in the world can listen for it, which is how one event reaches another.

options.subtitle: Own a lot of things for a long time

options.note: Red: one company. Blue: twenty. Press the green arrow on a pencil to draw another.

options.title: Diversifying, in three lines
options.caption: Click a pencil, change holdings, press Save.

options.title: A 1% fee looks small
options.note: That one percent takes 31% of the final amount. Compare expense ratios before you buy a fund.

options.eyebrow: WHY THE RED LINE IS BUMPIER
options.title: Most single stocks are risky
options.body: The model treats companies as independent. Real stocks tend to fall together, so diversifying helps less than this chart shows. It still helps. Returns here are invented, and real markets do lose money.

options.title: Take the match first
options.body: Many jobs match retirement contributions up to a limit. A 100% match doubles your money the day it goes in, before any market return. Skipping it is turning down part of your pay.

options.title: 14ft tall
options.body: 40 coins, each 4.8ft across at this scale.

options.title: 34ft tall
options.body: 100 coins, each 4.8ft across at this scale.

options.title: 69ft tall
options.body: 200 coins, each 4.8ft across at this scale.

options.title: 138ft tall
options.body: 400 coins, each 4.8ft across at this scale.

options.title: Your savings goal
options.intro: Menu > Create Model > Load Object > Draw. Paint the thing you are saving for and it inflates.

steps.text: Pick a real price and a monthly amount you could set aside.
Click your balloon, press Program, and repeat for each month you must save.
Inside the repeat: change size by 5 %, then wait 0.5 seconds.

options.tip: Months needed = price / monthly amount. Use that number in the repeat.

options.title: Your side business
options.intro: Build the stand, table or van you would run out of shapes, and then make it talk.

steps.text: Create Model: at least four pieces. Connect them, then Render Model.
What do you pay per sale? What do you charge? The gap is your profit.
Use forever, say and wait to announce the price, the cost and the profit.

options.tip: Remember Station 1: self-employed people pay both halves of FICA, 15.3%.
